author: implementation-agent

findings.summary: The index and article HTML render branches duplicate the same RenderableHtmlContent responsibility.
findings.consequence: Future changes to managed HTML rendering, event handling, or attributes can drift between the index and article views because the same component invocation is maintained in two branches that only differ by class and one inline style.
findings.evidence: Lines 228-234 render RenderableHtmlContent for the index with the same as, html, and click handler used again by the article branch starting on line 235; the only behavioral differences are class and style.
findings.recommendation: Replace the two RenderableHtmlContent branches with one v-else RenderableHtmlContent whose class is isIndex ? 'doc main' : 'content' and whose style is isIndex ? undefined : 'position:relative;'.
verification: Read RenderableHtmlContent.vue to confirm attrs and innerHTML handling are identical for both branches.
Read useManagedHtmlNavigation.ts to confirm both branches share the same click navigation behavior.
Inspected relevant presentation SSR and e2e tests covering index, article, loading, route transitions, and managed link navigation.

Inspected current source for app/pages/presentationer/[...segments].vue, its imported presentation-parser.ts and presentation-routes.ts dependencies, RenderableHtmlContent.vue, useManagedHtmlNavigation.ts, and relevant presentation tests discovered by rg.
